evidence.passage: Ghorani’s retrospective human analysis included 66 lung adenocarcinomas and 72 melanomas from The Cancer Genome Atlas, plus three immunotherapy-treated cohorts containing 131 melanoma patients in total and 31 with non-small-cell lung cancer. Mean DAI correlated with overall survival in three of five cohorts, with the reported effect for clonal rather than subclonal peptides. requirements.heading: The intuition
requirements.requirement: Receptor combinations vary between people and cells and depend on prior and local signals.

evidence.passage: Natural killer (NK) receptors are encoded in the germ line rather than assembled by the T-cell receptor’s somatic rearrangement process. They integrate complementary activating inputs with inhibitory signals; this is more complex than adding fixed on/off switches. Inhibitory motifs can recruit SHP phosphatases and suppress early activation, while several activating receptors signal through adaptors. Repertoire, receptor variants, prior education, cytokines and the target context matter. Some receptors also occur on T cells, and HLA-related recognition can depend on the bound peptide.

requirements.heading: Why it matters in cancer
requirements.requirement: HLA or B2M loss can lift inhibitory signals but killing still requires appropriate activation; avoid claiming every HLA-loss target is killed.

evidence.passage: Some inhibitory NK receptors recognize self HLA class I, while activating receptors respond to other features. Reduced self display can weaken an inhibitory input, but the NK cell, its prior education, activating signals and target context still determine the response. NK cells can also contribute antibody-dependent killing through Fc receptors. Donor-derived or engineered NK-cell products need their own compatibility, persistence and safety assessment rather than a blanket claim that matching or rejection never matters. The principle comes from mouse experiments: lymphoma cells selected for loss of H-2 were less malignant at low dose and were rejected by a non-adaptive mechanism, which suggested that natural killer cells are effectors in a defence system geared to detect reduced self MHC (Kärre et al., 1986); that does not guarantee the same outcome for any human tumour. MHC class I molecules are ligands for killer-cell immunoglobulin-like receptors (Parham, 2005): two-domain KIR2D receptors bind HLA-C alleles and three-domain KIR3D receptors bind HLA-A and HLA-B alleles, and the KIR family includes activating as well as inhibitory members (Mariuzza et al., 2025). CD94/NKG2A binds HLA-E, and HLA-E surface expression was enough to protect target cells from lysis by CD94/NKG2A-positive NK clones (Braud et al., 1998). NKG2D binds class I-related proteins including MICA, MICB and ULBP1 to 3 (Mariuzza et al., 2025), and engagement of NKG2D activated NK and gamma-delta T-cell cytolysis against epithelial tumour cells expressing MICA (Bauer et al., 1999). No single activating receptor dominates, since NK cells integrate synergistic signals from several (Long et al., 2013), and responsiveness depends on prior education: in human cell experiments, cytokine stimulation let hyporesponsive NK cells acquire KIR and function when the cognate MHC was present (Juelke et al., 2009). Loss of one HLA allele is not loss of all class I. Loss of beta-2 microglobulin removed surface class I in one of four relapsing melanoma patients (Zaretsky et al., 2016), and because HLA-E is assembled with beta-2 microglobulin, the KIR and NKG2A restraints would be expected to lift together; that last step is an inference not tested in the cited abstracts. A flow-based cytotoxicity assay that stains target and effector nuclei separately and distinguishes live from dead nuclei has been validated with NK-92 cells, CAR-T cells and tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (Rabinovich et al., 2019). Target death is not a count of effector cells that released granule contents: surface CD107a marked NK cells that degranulated after stimulation with MHC-devoid targets and correlated with lysis, and also marked a large subset that did not secrete cytokine, so different readouts count different cells (Alter et al., 2004). CD16 is a low-affinity Fc receptor for IgG that mediates antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity by NK cells (Liu, 2022), a route separate from missing-self recognition. Neither assay readout shows tumour entry or clinical benefit.

requirements.heading: The intuition
requirements.requirement: Treat subsets as adaptable differentiation programs rather than fixed job titles.

evidence.passage: CD4 T-cell subsets are differentiation programmes shaped by antigen recognition, cytokines and gene regulation. Conventional naive CD4 cells recognize peptide-HLA class II during priming, often on dendritic cells. Th1, Th2, Th17, follicular helper and regulatory programmes have characteristic signals, transcription factors and outputs, but these are not permanent job titles or mutually exclusive functional tests. The original Th1/Th2 distinction came from mouse clones in 1986; human tissue can contain mixed programmes.

requirements.heading: How it works
requirements.requirement: Explain T-cell antigen recognition, IFNg signaling, induced PD-L1 and PD-1-mediated restraint of the response.

evidence.passage: The sequence proposed by Taube and colleagues and mapped in more detail since is a loop. A T cell recognises a tumour peptide on HLA and releases interferon gamma; the interferon acts through the Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 in nearby tumour and immune cells; PD-L1 rises; PD-L1 binds PD-1 on the T cell and damps it. In melanoma cell lines, Garcia-Diaz and colleagues found that the interferon gamma, JAK1 and JAK2, STAT1, STAT2 and STAT3, IRF1 axis primarily regulates PD-L1, with IRF1 binding the PD-L1 promoter, and biopsies from patients with melanoma showed enrichment of that interferon signature and of STAT and IRF1 target genes in tumours that responded to anti-PD-1 treatment.

requirements.heading: How it works
requirements.requirement: Distinguish induced expression from tumor-intrinsic constitutive expression independent of local T-cell induction.

evidence.passage: Evidence from tissue. In human melanocytic lesions, 98% of PD-L1-positive (B7-H1-positive) tumours had tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes compared with 28% of PD-L1-negative tumours; positive melanocytes sat almost always immediately next to lymphocytes, and interferon gamma was detected at the interface but not in PD-L1-negative tumours (Taube and colleagues). The same colocalisation appeared in inflamed benign naevi, which fits PD-L1 as a response to tissue inflammation. In triple-negative breast cancer, Gruosso and colleagues described an immunoreactive group whose tumours had granzyme B-positive CD8 T cells inside cancer-cell regions, a type 1 interferon signature and elevated IDO and PD-L1, the pattern adaptive resistance predicts; that is an association in tissue and not a direct test of the loop. The alternative, called innate or constitutive resistance, is PD-L1 driven by the cancer cell's own signalling regardless of T cells.

evidence.passage: Evidence from tissue. evidence.passage: The claim. Immune surveillance concerns recognition and control of transformed cells. Immunoediting adds selection of the populations that persist. Elimination, equilibrium and escape are conceptual processes that can coexist or occur independently. Their assignment requires evidence of control, restraint or outgrowth and its mechanism; they are not a compulsory calendar for every clinical cancer. The immune system therefore both protects against cancer and shapes the cancers that emerge.

These associations do not prove the observed barrier caused resistance or that its removal helps a particular patient.

evidence.passage: Ghorani’s retrospective human analysis included 66 lung adenocarcinomas and 72 melanomas from The Cancer Genome Atlas, plus three immunotherapy-treated cohorts containing 131 melanoma patients in total and 31 with non-small-cell lung cancer. Mean DAI correlated with overall survival in three of five cohorts, with the reported effect for clonal rather than subclonal peptides. The authors reported evidence of superiority over nonsynonymous mutational and neoantigen burden in these analyses, not a universally superior clinical predictor. Mean DAI also correlated with immune-infiltration measures in melanoma (P = 0.027) and lung adenocarcinoma (P = 0.024), whereas mutational and neoantigen burden did not. The association with survival was not uniform: P = 0.068 in the TCGA melanoma cohort and P = 0.003 in one treated melanoma cohort. These population associations and the animal protection findings are different evidence tiers. Neither prospectively demonstrates that selecting a vaccine by DAI improves clinical outcomes.
